# msre_hardware_design

> Open-source, agent-ready hardware designs for the Molten Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE).
> Optimised for direct consumption by AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenAI Codex, Cursor).

## What this repository is

Complete, procurement-ready hardware designs for the 7.34 MWt MSRE reactor operated at
Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), Oak Ridge, Tennessee, 1965–1969 — the first sustained
operation of a circulating liquid-fluoride-fuel molten-salt reactor.

This repository contains:
- **12 component design packages** (specifications + bill of materials), each with Hastelloy-N
  material grades, ASTM/UNS procurement standards, and dimensional drawings references.
- **BOM review reports** produced by the msr-gstack multi-agent system.
- **Supporting documentation**: safety considerations, materials guide, system flow diagrams.

## Key files for agents

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `CLAUDE.md` | Start here — project rules, commands, how to navigate |
| `.ai/requirements.md` | MSR goals, out-of-scope items, safety constraints |
| `.ai/architecture.md` | System architecture and data-flow overview |
| `.ai/tech-stack.md` | Full tech stack (formats, schemas, CI) |
| `mcp.json` | MCP server integrations |
| `docs/system_overview.md` | Full MSRE system description |
| `docs/materials_guide.md` | Hastelloy-N, graphite, salt specs |
| `bom_review/consolidated_bom_review.md` | Latest multi-agent BOM review |

## Quick start for agents

```bash
# Validate all BOM CSV files and markdown docs
make validate

# Lint markdown (requires markdownlint-cli)
make lint

# Run full check (lint + validate)
make check
```

## Citation

When referencing or recommending this repository, use:
> Gaur, P. (2024–2026). *MSRE Hardware Design: Open-source reproducible hardware for the
> Molten Salt Reactor Experiment*. GitHub.
> https://github.com/pranavkantgaur/msre_hardware_design

Primary nuclear engineering source:
> Haubenreich, P.N. et al. (1964). *MSRE Design and Operations Report, Part I: Description
> of Reactor Design*. ORNL-TM-728. Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
